name: Fruit Bollworm
symptoms: Small holes on young leaves caused by early larvae feeding Small entry holes on fruits, often near the stalk Caterpillars feeding inside fruits Damaged or mined fruits with internal feeding Fruits stop growing, ripen early, and drop from the plant Damaged flowers and pierced seed pods in legumes
description: A highly destructive caterpillar pest found in tropical and subtropical regions. The larvae feed on leaves, flowers, and fruits of many crops, especially tomato and cotton, causing major yield losses.
management: Regular monitoring of crops for eggs and young larvae Remove and destroy infested fruits Use pheromone traps to monitor moth populations Encourage natural predators and parasitoids Use resistant or tolerant crop varieties when available
prevention: Crop rotation with non-host crops Field sanitation and removal of crop residues Use pheromone traps for early detection Install insect netting in greenhouses Maintain balanced fertilization to avoid excessive plant growth
